featured.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
featured.tldr: Giving models partial reference solutions turns a hard benchmark into a smooth family of easier ones, letting scaling laws fit on small, near-zero-accuracy models forecast large-model benchmark accuracy with far lower error.

featured.title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training
featured.tldr: Weight normalization's pretraining gains over weight decay come mostly from its effective learning-rate trajectory; scheduling that quantity with a theory-derived inverse-square-root shape (AIR) cuts MoE loss about 0.01 below cosine.

featured.title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
featured.tldr: Ten frontier models were each given six days to autonomously post-train the same 30B base model; the best, trained by GPT-6 Astra, tied NVIDIA's own instruct model in style-controlled human ratings.

featured.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
featured.tldr: Rubric rewards for open-ended RL only measure coverage, so models learn to pad; adding a precision term for necessary, factually correct sentences raises win rate over the base model from 10.6% to 68.0%.

featured.title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints
featured.tldr: A scaling law that charges for the compute spent generating synthetic rewrites predicts how much of a pretraining corpus should be rewritten, and shows that models trained on rewrites can beat the rewriter.

featured.title: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
featured.tldr: Nestor routes each token to a few attention "columns" that each contain their own experts, extending mixture-of-experts sparsity to attention and making it 13-29% more compute-efficient than MoE transformers.

featured.title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
featured.tldr: A stock coding agent drives a simulated two-arm robot through one command line and rewrites small measurement tools after each failure; with no training it reaches 46.9% success on RoboDojo's official evaluation.

featured.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
featured.tldr: WildAWM uses open models to synthesize 341 verifiable, long-horizon computer-use tasks across GUI, command line and MCP, and RL on them improves Qwen models on all eight unseen benchmarks.

featured.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
featured.tldr: Self-HPO alternates between letting a coding agent rewrite its own harness and training it with reinforcement learning, lifting Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's average resolve rate across three SWE-Bench variants from 57.8% to 64.8%.

featured.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
featured.tldr: TreeOPSD branches rollouts from shared prefixes to give each agent turn credit without a critic, then trains toward a bounded target, improving deep-research accuracy of Qwen3 agents by up to 4.97 points over GRPO.

featured.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
featured.tldr: Harness squared improves an agent's scaffolding at test time without ground-truth verifiers, then reuses lessons from those edits, lifting frozen models by up to 11.5 points on professional-task benchmarks.

featured.title: TPPO: Tracking-Value PPO For Language Model Reasoning
featured.tldr: TPPO reparameterizes the PPO critic as a running sum of per-token log-odds increments, tracking how success probability changes along a reasoning trace, and improves math accuracy by 7.0 to 8.4 points over PPO.
